newsitem.title: FRANCE: ALPINE SKIING-SYKORA MOVES CLOSE TO SLALOM WIN.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-SYKORA MOVES CLOSE TO SLALOM WIN.

text.p: Austrian Thomas Sykora moved close to his fourth victory this winter by clocking the fastest time in the first leg of a World Cup slalom on Sunday.

Sykora, who won three of the four races staged so far and finished second in the other, skied faultlessly through the 72 gates of the piste in the French Alps resort of Chamonix to set a best time of 57.58 seconds.
Nobody could follow that pace, not even great Italian Alberto Tomba, who was over one second slower with the second fastest time in 58.74.
Some doubt had been cast on Tomba's participation after he halted training in Italy on Wednesday because of a flare-up of pain in the wrist which he injured in a fall last October.
He eventually decided to take part but said after the first leg that he had flu and was not sure of starting the second leg.
Frenchman Yves Dimier, chasing his first top three placing this season, had the third fastest time in 58.75.
The slalom and Saturday's downhill here won by Italian Kristian Ghedina count for the winter's first combined event.
